message.content:
`docker start` is used to start **containers**, not the Docker daemon itself.  
To bring the Docker service up on Windows you have a few options:

| Method | How to do it |
|--------|--------------|
| **Docker Desktop** | Open the Docker Desktop app from the Start menu (or double‑click the icon). It will automatically start the Docker Engine. |
| **PowerShell** | Run `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` (requires admin rights). |
| **Command Prompt** | Run `net start com.docker.service` (requires admin rights). |
| **SC command** | Run `sc start com.docker.service` (requires admin rights). |
| **Docker Machine** (if you’re using it) | Run `docker-machine start default` and then `docker-machine env default` to set the environment variables. |

After starting the service, you can verify that Docker is running with:

```powershell
docker info
```

or

```powershell
docker version
```

If you want to start a specific container after the daemon is up, you can use:

```powershell
docker start <container_name_or_id>
```

or start all stopped containers:

```powershell
docker start $(docker ps -aq)
```

Let me know if you need help with any of those steps!
